objective: Run short code-rework, readonly, and no-change tasks through the formal CLI on the Batch 1a durable skeleton, while ensuring corrections and pause/cancel input cannot be crossed by stale evidence or completion proposals.

implementation.provider: DeepSeek through BoundedToolTurnClient with retry_limit=2 and fallback_allowed=false
implementation.business_attempt_exit: Four consecutive settled attempts for the same stable blocker without relevant progress produce STALLED.
implementation.review_disagreement_exit: Three complete independent-review disagreements for the same outcome produce WAITING_INPUT.

implemented_rules: The launcher, interpreter, configuration, runtime state, and business workspaces are physically rooted in the marked development checkout; forbidden source roots are never write targets.
The manifest declares one persistent state authority root, so changing --state-root cannot split live ownership or forget UNKNOWN responsibility for the same workspace.
One inter-process authority lease is acquired before provider-home, Backend, control socket, or business workspace initialization; live status/input route through the authority socket.
Provider calls, tool calls, program checks, and reviewer calls are persisted as Loop operations with request/result identity and effect status.
All evidence handoffs inherit an immutable task binding. Goal, acceptance, handled-input, artifact, execution, or run changes invalidate the old stage before the next effect or commit.
readonly/no_change mutation attempts are denied before actual tool dispatch regardless of the general write approval flag.
Code checks run only with the pinned Python interpreter against a read-only copied input in macOS Seatbelt and a dedicated writable output; unsupported execution is NOT_RUN and waits for input.
Code completion accepts either a verified change or an initially-correct zero diff. Both use the same fixed program check and a strict artifact-bound independent JSON review.
Runtime completion directly evaluates the same AcceptanceCase/CaseObservation contract through LoopAcceptanceEvaluator used by scoring; only CASE_PASS may be submitted as success.
CORRECTION/MESSAGE, PAUSE, and CANCEL are durable inputs accepted during long Provider/check/review work. Stale results remain traceable but cannot approve the newer binding.

Cancellation retains completed effects, captures the current workspace artifact, prevents success submission, and records a unique CANCELLED terminal. Repeated CANCEL rebinding is safe; UNKNOWN effects instead return bounded recovery_blocked with ownership retained.
Structured program progress is accepted only from the exact SITINA_LOOP_CHECK_PROGRESS_V1 schema with stable requirement identities and a true satisfied/remaining set reduction.

verified_rules.evidence: Boundary probe and authority tests verify the isolated marked checkout, pinned interpreter, unique state authority, read-only credential reference, and pre-initialization rejection.
Live DeepSeek formal CLI cases verify readonly facts (46, zero diff), fixed-check code rework (FAIL to PASS), and initially-correct code (PASS with zero diff).

The formal correction case invalidates an in-flight old reviewer and succeeds in cycle 2 on goal_version 2. Formal PAUSE remains nonterminal and unchanged; formal CANCEL retains a completed write, cancels success, captures the current artifact, and creates one terminal event.

Race tests cover corrections after goal read, before check binding, during check/review, after review verdict, and in the acceptance commit gap. Repeated cancel in the terminal gap is rebound; UNKNOWN cancellation exits recovery_blocked without retrying terminalization.

A six-cycle runner test proves one structured requirement reduction resets only the consecutive no-progress count and four later irrelevant changes produce STALLED; a separate test preserves the three-review-disagreement WAITING_INPUT threshold. This is check-owned structured progress, not full semantic R11 review.
Every successful formal case records SITINA_LOOP_CASE_EVALUATION_V1 with outcome CASE_PASS in both the acceptance details and terminal result.

implemented_but_not_fully_verified: The control socket isolates disconnected/partial clients and uses a short Darwin-safe path; tests cover these cases, but prolonged hostile-client load is outside this batch.

Provider transport failure is persisted and docks WAITING_INPUT after bounded transport retries; a historical real Provider worker failure exercised it, while the final live Provider cases exercised successful transport.
Cancellation artifact capture is verified for known completed effects and UNKNOWN produces a bounded recovery report; actual effect reconciliation remains a later recovery feature.
unimplemented_items: Batch 2 bounded long-context assembly, historical query, and continued long-input processing.
Batch 3 full background lifecycle, process restart/reconnect, execution identity continuation, and UNKNOWN effect reconciliation.
Batch 4 general Skill/dependency candidate testing, Journal publication, projection, and ordinary-new-session consumption.

Batch 6 complete experience candidate inventory, item-by-item disposition, parent-obligation rebuild, and new-task benefit.
Batch 7 long-running end-to-end tasks, mid-course correction across recovery, visual artifact verification, and full first-release acceptance.

General semantic progress adjudication, independent review of ambiguous progress claims, and complex multi-action attempt ownership. Batch 1b verifies only stable IDs emitted by the fixed program check.
Program-check executors other than the pinned Python interpreter. They return NOT_RUN rather than being executed unsafely.
Computer use and visual/TCC validation, which the current specification explicitly defers.
historical_evidence_policy: Runs under runtime/r4-loop-dev/state/real-* and superseded canonical experiments remain as debugging history. They are not counted as final formal evidence after the unique state-authority rule; replacements are named in formal-cli-evidence.json.
conclusion: Batch 1b meets its short-task formal-entry objective in the isolated development checkout. It does not claim the complete Sitina first release, full recovery, memory, Skills publication, long-task, or visual acceptance, and it performs no production cutover.
